prompt: I want to test how you verify edits. First, create a brand-new .pen scratch document with a single LoginCard frame containing: a 'Sign in' heading, an Email input, a Password input, a primary 'Sign in' button (blue fill), and a 'Forgot password?' link below the button. Once that's in place, perform this edit: change the Sign in button's fill to a brand green color, and add 8px of paddingTop to the link's container so it has more breathing room. After the edit, explain — step by step — exactly which MCP tools you called to verify the edit landed correctly, in what order, and why you chose each. Be precise about which nodeId you passed to each verification call.

assertions.text: Agent identifies the specific node IDs to edit before issuing the batch_design call — either by capturing them from prior batch_design construction response bindings (the preferred approach) or via an explicit batch_get lookup on the LoginCard subtree
Describes performing both edit ops (fill change + paddingTop) in a single batch_design call
Calls snapshot_layout scoped to the LoginCard (parentId is the card node, NOT the document root or page) to confirm paddingTop landed
Calls batch_get on the button node to confirm fill resolved to a variable reference (not a raw hex color)
States exactly 1 get_screenshot call in the edit phase, scoped to the LoginCard nodeId (not document root or page frame)
Does NOT describe re-screenshotting in dark mode (the change is a variable-bound color + structural, not mode-conditional)
